answers.quote: Their first attack during his reign was repulsed by prince Skandagupta.
answers.notes: Claim c61: towards the later part of Kumaragupta's reign the Hunas crossed the Hindukush; their first attack was repulsed by prince Skandagupta.

answers.answer: হূণ শাসক তোরমাণের পুত্র ও উত্তরসূরি
answers.quote: The first important ruler of the Hunas in India was Toramana who conquered an area stretching up to Eran near Bhopal in central India. His son Mihirkula succeeded him in AD 515.
answers.notes: Claim c62: Toramana was the first important Huna ruler in India; his son Mihirkula (Mihirakula) succeeded him in AD 515.

answers.answer: মালবের যশোধর্মণ ও গুপ্ত রাজা নরসিংহগুপ্ত বালাদিত্য
answers.quote: Both Yashodharman of Malwa and Narasimhagupta Baladitya of the Gupta dynasty finally defeated Mihirkula. But this victory over the Hunas could not revive the Gupta Empire.
answers.notes: Claim c63 names exactly Yashodharman of Malwa and the Gupta king Narasimhagupta Baladitya as those who finally defeated Mihirakula.

answers.quote: The first evidence of sati (immolation of widow) is found in an inscription (AD 510) at Eran in Madhya Pradesh.
answers.notes: Claim c64 gives the first sati evidence as the AD 510 inscription at Eran, Madhya Pradesh.

answers.quote: The other famous dramatists to have flourished in this period are Shudraka, writer of Mrichchhkatikam and Vishakhadatta who authored Mudrarakshasa.
answers.notes: Claim c65: Shudraka wrote the Mrichchhakatika; Vishakhadatta (a distractor option) authored the Mudrarakshasa instead.

answers.quote: Another text written by him is Kadambari.
answers.notes: Claim c66: Banabhatta, Harsha's court poet who wrote the Harshacharita, also wrote the Kadambari ('him' in the verbatim quote refers to Banabhatta per the claim text).

answers.quote: He made Ujjain as the second capital of the Empire.
answers.notes: Claim c67: after his conquest of western India, Chandragupta II made Ujjain the second capital of the Gupta Empire.

answers.quote: After this victory, he performed the horse sacrifice and assumed the title ‘ Sakari’ meaning destroyer of Sakas.
answers.notes: Claim c68: after defeating Rudrasimha III, the last Saka Kshatrapa ruler, Chandragupta II assumed the title 'Sakari' (destroyer of the Sakas).

answers.quote: The Nalanda University founded by Kumaragupta I became the most celebrated Buddhist educational centre in North India.
answers.notes: Claim c69 states Nalanda University was founded by Kumaragupta I.

answers.quote: The other famous dramatists to have flourished in this period are Shudraka, writer of Mrichchhkatikam and Vishakhadatta who authored Mudrarakshasa.
answers.notes: Pair 2 correct and pair 3 wrong per claim c65 (Mudrarakshasa is by Vishakhadatta, not Kalidasa); pair 1 correct per claim c66 (Banabhatta also wrote the Kadambari, NIOS Lesson 7, p. 111). Hence only pairs 1 and 2 are correct.
